claim_1.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at baseline days -7, 0, and 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed that many B cell subsets had low within-subject variability over more than two months compared to their inter-subject variability.

sources.section: Substantial immune baseline variations in healthy subjects
sources.quote: Among populations with high overall variability, many B cell subsets showed low within-subject variability (and therefore high temporal stability) over a period of more than two months (indicated in dark gray in Figure 2A).

comparison.finding: many B cell subsets showed low within-subject variability between day -7 and day 0
many B cell subsets showed low within-subject variability between day 0 and day 70, indicating high temporal stability over more than two months

claim_3.claim: ELISpot analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals 7 days after vaccination (day 7) showed increased influenza vaccine-specific IgG+ antibody secreting cells compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Coherent changes in immune parameters post-vaccination
sources.quote: As expected, we observed strong, but highly variable, increases in influenza vaccine-specific IgG+ antibody secreting cells on day 7 (Figure 3A).

comparison.finding: influenza vaccine-specific IgG+ antibody secreting cells increased on day 7 compared to baseline

claim_6.claim: Flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals 1 day after vaccination (day 1) showed coherent increases in innate immune cell populations, including CD40+ and CD86+ monocytes and IFNα+ plasmacytoid DCs, compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Coherent changes in immune parameters post-vaccination
sources.quote: Again, day 1 changes reflected activation of innate immune cells, including CD40+ and CD86+ monocytes (ID65 and ID67) and IFNa+ plasmacytoid DCs (ID78), populations that have been linked to vaccination efficacy and responses to influenza (Fonteneau et al., 2003; van Duin et al., 2007).

comparison.finding: day 1 showed coherent increases in innate immune cell populations, including CD40+ and CD86+ monocytes and IFNα+ plasmacytoid DCs, compared to baseline

claim_7.claim: Flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals 1 day after vaccination (day 1) showed coherent changes in adaptive cell populations, particularly activated CD8+ and CD4+ T cells and both naïve and memory B cells, compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Coherent changes in immune parameters post-vaccination
sources.quote: However, we also observed changes in adaptive cell populations, particularly those reflecting activation of CD8+ and CD4+ T cells, as well as both naïve and memory B cells (Kaminski et al., 2012).

comparison.finding: adaptive cell populations changed at day 1 versus baseline, particularly activated CD8+ and CD4+ T cells and both naïve and memory B cells

claim_8.claim: Flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals 7 days after vaccination (day 7) showed coherent changes primarily in adaptive cell populations, including plasmablasts, a related CD20+CD27+CD38+ B-cell subset, and activated T-cell populations, compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Coherent changes in immune parameters post-vaccination
sources.quote: Day 7 responses primarily reflected changes in adaptive cell populations, including plasmablasts (ID87) as expected, but also a related CD20+ B subset that expressed CD27 and CD38 (ID96, Figure S3), as well as activated T cell populations.

comparison.finding: day 7 showed coherent changes in adaptive cell populations relative to baseline, including plasmablasts, a related CD20+CD27+CD38+ B-cell subset, and activated T-cell populations

claim_10.claim: Flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from healthy individuals grouped by baseline serologic and memory B-cell status showed that the more naïve group had greater increases in plasmablast frequencies on day 7 after vaccination (day 7) compared to the group with higher baseline serologic and memory B-cell values.

sources.section: Antibody titer and cellular responses depend on pre-vaccination serological state
sources.quote: However, the more naïve group exhibited significantly greater increases in plasmablasts (ID87) and seasonal vaccine-specific ELISpot responses on day 7 (Figure 4C).

groups.cohort: group with higher baseline serologic and memory B-cell values

comparison.finding: the more naïve group had greater increases in plasmablast frequencies on day 7 compared to the group with higher baseline serologic and memory B-cell values

claim_11.claim: ELISpot analysis of PBMCs from healthy individuals grouped by baseline serologic and memory B-cell status showed that the more naïve group had greater seasonal vaccine-specific IgG responses on day 7 after vaccination (day 7) compared to the group with higher baseline serologic and memory B-cell values.

sources.section: Antibody titer and cellular responses depend on pre-vaccination serological state
sources.quote: However, the more naïve group exhibited significantly greater increases in plasmablasts (ID87) and seasonal vaccine-specific ELISpot responses on day 7 (Figure 4C).

groups.cohort: group with higher baseline serologic and memory B-cell values

comparison.finding: the more naïve group had greater seasonal vaccine-specific IgG ELISpot responses on day 7 after vaccination than the group with higher baseline serologic and memory B-cell values

claim_14.claim: Flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals 7 days after vaccination (day 7) showed that plasmablasts and the overlapping CD20+IgD-CD27+CD38+ B-cell subpopulation were the dominant cellular contributors to prediction of day 70 antibody titer responses compared to other measured cell populations.

sources.section: Identification of post-vaccination predictors and robust correlates
sources.quote: Accordingly, plasmablasts (ID87) and the overlapping CD20+ subpopulation (ID96) were the dominant cellular contributors (Figure 5E) (Withers et al., 2007).

comparison.finding: plasmablasts and the overlapping CD20+IgD-CD27+CD38+ B-cell subpopulation at day 7 were the dominant cellular contributors predicting day 70 antibody titer responses compared to other measured cell populations

claim_17.claim: Flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at baseline (day 0) showed that predictive models of adjusted and unadjusted day 70 antibody titer responses could be built using cell population frequencies alone compared to models integrating pathway/transcript data with cell populations, which performed substantially worse.

sources.section: Identification of pre-vaccination predictors and correlates
sources.quote: Notably, predictive models could be built by using cell populations alone (Figure 6B)—integrating pathway/transcript with cell population data performed substantially worse (best median AUC was 0.6 vs. 0.78 using cell populations alone). Thus, day 0 cell frequencies alone provided the essential information for prediction.

claim_18.claim: Flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at baseline (day 0) showed that adjusted day 70 antibody titer responses were predicted by twelve cell populations including memory, naïve and transitional B cells, CD4 effector memory T cells, IFNα+ myeloid dendritic cells, and several activated T-cell populations compared to unadjusted maximum fold-change, for which primarily T-cell subsets contributed.

sources.section: Identification of pre-vaccination predictors and correlates
sources.quote: Twelve cell populations were identified for adjMFC, including memory, naïve and transitional B cells, CD4 effector memory T cells, IFNα+ myeloid dendritic cells (mDC), and several activated T cell populations (Figure 6C; see Methods).

sources.section: Identification of pre-vaccination predictors and correlates
sources.quote: Only some of these populations, primarily the T cell subsets, contributed to the prediction of MFC (Figure 6C). Thus, by accounting for baseline serology using adjMFC, we uncovered additional baseline predictors.

claim_19.claim: Flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at baseline days -7, 0, and 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed that, except for CD86+IgD+ memory B cells, the predictive B-cell populations and some predictive CD4+ T-cell populations were remarkably stable within individuals over more than two months compared to their inter-subject variability.

sources.section: Temporal stability of predictive cell populations
sources.quote: Except for ID105 (CD86+IgD+ memory B cells), all of the B cell and some of the CD4+ T cell (including effector memory) predictive populations were remarkably stable within individuals over a period of more than two months (Figure 6D).

comparison.finding: predictive B-cell populations and some predictive CD4+ T-cell populations were stable within individuals from day -7 to day 0; CD86+IgD+ memory B cells were the exception
predictive B-cell populations and some predictive CD4+ T-cell populations were stable within individuals from day 0 to day 70; CD86+IgD+ memory B cells were the exception

claim_20.claim: Flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at baseline days -7, 0, and 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed that stable CD38+ B-cell populations ID91, ID96, ID103, and ID108 contributed to prediction of adjusted day 70 antibody titer responses but not unadjusted maximum fold-change compared to less stable or nonpredictive populations.

sources.section: Temporal stability of predictive cell populations
sources.quote: These stable B-cell populations (ID91, 96, 103, 108) were all CD38+ and contributed to the prediction of adjMFC but not MFC.

comparison.finding: stable CD38+ B-cell populations ID91, ID96, ID103, and ID108 contributed to prediction of adjusted day 70 antibody titer responses but not unadjusted maximum fold-change

claim_21.claim: Flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals across days -7, 0, 1, 7, and 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed that predictive cell populations remained able to separate high and low adjusted responders over time compared to each other.

sources.section: Temporal stability of predictive cell populations
sources.quote: Examining the predictive cell populations' temporal profile further confirmed their stability and ability to separate the high and low responders (Figures 6E, 6F and S5).

comparison.finding: predictive cell populations separated high and low adjusted responders at day -7
predictive cell populations separated high and low adjusted responders at day 0
predictive cell populations separated high and low adjusted responders at day 1
predictive cell populations separated high and low adjusted responders at day 7
predictive cell populations separated high and low adjusted responders at day 70

claim_22.claim: Flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals across days -7, 0, 1, 7, and 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed that the predictive B-cell population ID96 increased coherently on day 7 after vaccination (day 7) and returned to lower levels by day 70 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Temporal stability of predictive cell populations
sources.quote: This was true even for ID96, which increased coherently across subjects at day 7 post-vaccination and returned to lower levels by day 70.

comparison.finding: predictive B-cell population ID96 increased coherently on day 7 relative to baseline
predictive B-cell population ID96 returned to lower levels by day 70 after increasing at day 7

claim_23.claim: Flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at baseline (day 0) showed that adjusted day 70 antibody titer responses could still be robustly predicted using only the 56 most stable cell populations compared to models using less stable populations.

sources.section: Temporal stability of predictive cell populations
sources.quote: Even using a smaller k of 10 (versus 30 previously), adjMFC could be robustly predicted (median AUC=0.78; Figure 6G).

sources.section: Temporal stability of predictive cell populations
sources.quote: As expected, the populations contributing most to adjMFC prediction were the same stable ones identified above. Thus, the less stable populations were not essential for adjMFC prediction.

claim_24.claim: Flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at baseline (day 0) showed that stable cell populations decreased predictive performance for unadjusted maximum fold-change compared to adjusted maximum fold-change, indicating that transient signals provided most of the predictive power for unadjusted responses.

sources.section: Temporal stability of predictive cell populations
sources.quote: In contrast, use of the stable cell populations decreased the predictive performance for MFC, which remained flat for all values of k.

sources.section: Temporal stability of predictive cell populations
sources.quote: Thus, the more transient signals provided the bulk of the predictive power for MFC, whereas that for adjMFC came from temporally stable parameters that may have captured the unique immune-status of individuals.

claim_25.claim: Flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals showed that models trained on day 0 cell-population data accurately predicted adjusted day 70 antibody titer responses using independent baseline measurements from day -7 and day 70 compared to chance.

sources.section: Temporal stability of predictive cell populations
sources.quote: Highly accurate prediction could still be made for all k's, e.g., AUC=0.91 and AUC=0.86 for days -7 and 70 using k=10, respectively. Thus, the predictive signals were remarkably stable over time.

comparison.finding: models trained on day 0 cell-population data accurately predicted adjusted day 70 antibody titer responses using independent baseline measurements from day -7 compared to chance
models trained on day 0 cell-population data accurately predicted adjusted day 70 antibody titer responses using independent measurements from day 70 compared to chance

claim_2.claim: Microarrays analysis of PBMCs from healthy individuals at baseline (day 0) showed substantial transcript abundance variation across subjects compared to within-subject baseline variation over days -7, 0, and 70 for many genes and pathways.

sources.section: Substantial immune baseline variations in healthy subjects
sources.quote: Transcript abundance for day 0 PBMCs also showed substantial variation (Figure 2B), likely reflecting in part the different proportions of cell subsets among subjects.

sources.section: Substantial immune baseline variations in healthy subjects
sources.quote: Assessment of inter-vs. intra-subject variation demonstrated diverse patterns, with subject-to-subject baseline differences (blue bars) contributing substantially to the observed variability of many genes and pathways (Figures 2B and C).

claim_4.claim: Microarrays analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals 1 day after vaccination (day 1) showed coherent gene-expression changes enriched for innate immune-cell activation pathways, including Interferon-related genes, compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Coherent changes in immune parameters post-vaccination
sources.quote: Overall, day 1 responses included pathways reflecting innate immune-cell activation, including Interferon-related genes, as observed by others (Bucasas et al., 2011; Nakaya et al., 2011; Obermoser et al., 2013) (Figure 3C and Table S3).

comparison.finding: day 1 showed coherent gene-expression changes enriched for innate immune-cell activation pathways, including Interferon-related genes, compared to baseline

claim_5.claim: Microarrays analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals 7 days after vaccination (day 7) showed coherent gene-expression changes enriched for adaptive pathways, including Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) stress and N-glycan biosynthesis, compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Coherent changes in immune parameters post-vaccination
sources.quote: By day 7, adaptive pathways were more predominant, including those strongly associated with plasmablasts, such as “Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) stress” and “N-glycan biosynthesis” (see below) (Gass et al., 2004; Iwakoshi et al., 2003).

comparison.finding: By day 7, coherent gene-expression changes were enriched for adaptive pathways, including Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) stress and N-glycan biosynthesis, compared to baseline

claim_9.claim: Microneutralization assay analysis of serum from 63 healthy individuals at day 70 after vaccination showed that subjects with higher initial titers had lower fold-changes in titers compared to subjects with lower initial titers.

sources.section: Antibody titer and cellular responses depend on pre-vaccination serological state
sources.quote: Interestingly, subjects with higher initial titers tended to have lower fold-changes.

comparison.finding: subjects with higher initial titers had lower fold-changes in titers than subjects with lower initial titers

claim_12.claim: Microarrays analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals 1 day after vaccination (day 1), using pathway enrichment analysis, showed that Interferon Signaling robustly correlated with maximum fold-change in day 70 antibody titers compared to pathways that were not robust correlates.

sources.section: Identification of post-vaccination predictors and robust correlates
sources.quote: While models built using either gene expression or cell populations from day 1 were not predictive, “Interferon Signaling” correlated robustly with MFC (Figure 5C).

comparison.finding: Interferon Signaling at day 1 robustly correlated with maximum fold-change in day 70 antibody titers

claim_13.claim: Microarrays analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals 7 days after vaccination (day 7) showed that highly predictive models of both adjusted and unadjusted day 70 antibody titer responses could be built from day 7 gene-expression data compared to day 1 gene-expression data, which were not predictive.

sources.section: Identification of post-vaccination predictors and robust correlates
sources.quote: In contrast, highly predictive models could be built using day 7 data for both adjMFC and MFC (Figures 5D).

sources.section: Identification of post-vaccination predictors and robust correlates
sources.quote: While models built using either gene expression or cell populations from day 1 were not predictive, “Interferon Signaling” correlated robustly with MFC (Figure 5C).

comparison.finding: day 7 gene-expression data built highly predictive models of adjusted and unadjusted day 70 antibody titer responses, whereas day 1 gene-expression data were not predictive

claim_15.claim: Microarrays analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at baseline (day 0), using pathway enrichment analysis, showed that neither day 0 gene expression nor pathway activity alone was predictive of adjusted or unadjusted day 70 antibody titer responses compared to baseline cell-frequency models.

sources.section: Identification of pre-vaccination predictors and correlates
sources.quote: Neither day 0 gene expression nor pathway activity (defined in Figure S2C) alone was predictive of either endpoint, although a number of robustly correlated genes and pathways could be identified (Figure 6A).

claim_16.claim: Microarrays analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at baseline (day 0), using pathway enrichment analysis, showed that genes associated with pattern recognition and Interferon signaling robustly correlated with maximum fold-change in day 70 antibody titers compared to adjusted maximum fold-change.

sources.section: Identification of pre-vaccination predictors and correlates
sources.quote: Notably, genes associated with pattern recognition and Interferon signaling robustly correlated to MFC, but less so to adjMFC.

claim_26.claim: Microarrays analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals 7 days after vaccination (day 7) showed that the predictive and coherently changing cell populations ID87 and ID96 were linked to antigen secreting cell/B cell/plasmablast-specific genes including Ig chains, XBP1, and IRF4 compared to non-plasmablast-associated genes.

sources.section: Transcriptomic signature of the predictive cell populations
sources.quote: As expected, the two predictive and coherently changing cell populations from day 7 (ID87 and ID96) were linked to known antigen secreting cell/B cell/plasmablast-specific genes, including Ig chains, XBP1 and IRF4, as well as plasmablast-associated pathways such as ER stress (Figures 7B and D).

claim_27.claim: Microarrays analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals 7 days after vaccination (day 7) showed that the predictive and coherently changing cell populations ID87 and ID96 were associated with plasmablast-related pathways including ER stress and N-glycan biosynthesis compared to pathways not associated with these populations.

sources.section: Transcriptomic signature of the predictive cell populations
sources.quote: As expected, the two predictive and coherently changing cell populations from day 7 (ID87 and ID96) were linked to known antigen secreting cell/B cell/plasmablast-specific genes, including Ig chains, XBP1 and IRF4, as well as plasmablast-associated pathways such as ER stress (Figures 7B and D).

sources.section: Transcriptomic signature of the predictive cell populations
sources.quote: These populations were also associated with N-glycan biosynthesis, consistent with the highly glycosylated state of immunoglobulins and the requirement for proper glycosylation for plasma cell development (Tulp et al., 1986).

claim_28.claim: Microarrays analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at baseline (day 0) showed that mitochondria-related pathways were positively associated with the predictive CD38+ naïve B-cell population ID108 and CD38hi transitional B-cell population ID91 compared to other predictive populations.

sources.section: Transcriptomic signature of the predictive cell populations
sources.quote: Several mitochondria-related pathways were positively associated with ID108 (CD38+ naïve B cells) and ID91 (CD38hi transitional B cells), perhaps reflecting changes in bioenergetic states associated with B cell development and activation.

claim_29.claim: Microarrays analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at baseline (day 0) showed that innate pathways including PRR signaling, TREM1 signaling, and interferon-related genes were positively linked to IL22+ and IL2+ CD4+ T cells and negatively linked to effector memory CD4+ T cells and perforin+ CD8+ cells compared to those other adaptive subsets.

sources.section: Transcriptomic signature of the predictive cell populations
sources.quote: Of note, several innate pathways (PRR signaling, TREM1 signaling, and interferon-related genes) were positively linked to IL22+ and IL2+ CD4+ T cells (ID25 and ID26), and negatively linked to ID36 and ID50.

claim_30.claim: Microarrays analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals showed that the predictive B-cell population ID96 had largely distinct transcriptomic signatures at baseline (day 0) and 7 days after vaccination (day 7) compared to itself across those two timepoints.

sources.section: Transcriptomic signature of the predictive cell populations
sources.quote: Interestingly, ID96, a day 0 predictive B-cell population that also coherently increased on day 7 (Figures 3D and 6F), showed largely distinct signatures on days 0 and 7 (Figures 7A-D), suggesting differences in the cell population defined by those markers, or distinct functional interactions with other cell populations post-vaccination.

comparison.finding: the predictive B-cell population ID96 showed largely distinct transcriptomic signatures between day 0 and day 7
